title: Regional triage circuit orchestrator for latency-tiered geo pinning and proportional shedding
creator: Avery Chen
description: Implement a regional triage circuit orchestrator that combines latency-tiered routing, geo pinning with soft affinity, and capacity-aware proportional shedding. Goals: 1) keep user-visible tail latency within SLOs (P50/P95/P99 targets per region) during regional degradation, 2) gracefully shed load while preserving high-value traffic, 3) provide a deterministic failover that prefers low-latency regions but respects capacity and data residency constraints. The controller will emit signals to the request director: latency_hints, capacity_credits, and pinned_affinity. It will also drive local circuit breakers (reject/open/half-open) with staged thresholds and contribute to a global shed budget to avoid mass failovers.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes per-region latency tiers and adjusts routing weights within 5s of observed shift
Pinning mechanism respects customer geo constraints and can be overridden by emergency unlock policy
Circuit breaker transitions are logged and replayable via trace IDs; rollback to closed state possible via automated half-open probes
In synthetic load tests, when a region's available GPU tokens drop by 40% the orchestrator reduces routed traffic to that region proportionally and keeps global P95 within 1.25x baseline
Dashboards show per-region latency tiers, circuit breaker status, shed rate, and customer impact indicators
testing_plan: Phase 1 unit tests for decision logic and hysteresis. Phase 2 integration tests with the request director stub and synthetic token bucket to simulate capacity evaporation. Phase 3 chaos runbook: simulate region slowdowns (CPU/GPU saturation, network egress instability) and validate shed rates, failover correctness, and SLO preservation. All tests automated in CI; load tests run against staging cluster with canary traffic matching production shape.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged rollout to staging. 2) Canary in production on 5% of traffic for low-impact orgs for 24h. 3) Evaluate metrics and run blast radius plan. 4) Gradually expand to 25%/50%/100% with 2-hour observation windows. Emergency kill switch via console and /admin API.
risks: Over-eager shedding may disproportionately affect small customers; mitigation: prioritize high-value tokens and maintain fairness heuristics
Incorrect latency tiering during short-lived spikes could cause churn; mitigation: apply sliding windows and minimum observation periods
Complex interactions with existing autoscaler may cause oscillation; mitigation: add damping and coordination signals to autoscaler team
decisions: Use exponential backoff for half-open probe frequency to avoid probe storms
Represent capacity as a normalized credit score (0-1) per region and translate to proportional routing weight reductions
Pinning is soft by default; hard pinning requires an org-level policy flag and audit log entry

notes: We intentionally decoupled routing weight adjustments from immediate autoscaler scale-up decisions to avoid feedback loops. The orchestrator will emit a 'preferred_capacity_request' metric rather than direct scaling ops; Autoscaler team will consume this with a 30s smoothing window.
